proposals.answer: Every play, skill and agent that builds the software, and every context sub-agent it starts, is a build play for the check. Only /shape-slice (which writes the hidden file into the evals folder), /shape-eval and the eval itself may name the evals folder.
proposals.context: The eval capability's page says no builder, no skill that builds the software and no context sub-agent reads the plan's evals folder. The /shape-slice feature page (fn-795, line 4) says /shape-slice writes the slice's hidden file into that folder, so it is one of the plays that may name it.

The evidence-file template (core/memory/standards/templates/evidence-file.md, lines 35-38) records each run's session and its ledger in the run's evidence file, but no model page, memory line or earlier answer names where the product owner must see the flag.
proposals.why: No source names the place, so the product owner sets it; the question keeps its assumption.

proposals.answer: Yes. Change the proof line 'The eval is kept in a place where no builder can read it.' to 'No builder is given the eval, and a check flags each build session that read the evals folder.'
